bibl.title: Hippocampal CA1 and CA3 neural recording in the human brain: validation of depth electrode placement through high-resolution imaging and electrophysiology

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In this study we demonstrate a combined imaging and electrophysiological recording methodology that successfully confirms electrode placement within the CA1 and CA3 subfields of the human hippocampus without requiring postoperative histological confirmation.

span.label: localization of single-neuron recordings in human hippocampal CA1 and CA3
span.quote: In this paper, verified localization of singly recorded hippocampal neurons within the CA3 and CA1 cell fields is demonstrated.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Macro-micro depth electrodes were implanted in 23 human patients undergoing invasive monitoring for identification of epileptic seizure foci.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Monosynaptic Schaffer collateral transmission from CA3 to CA1 produces the 2-5 msec lagged firing correlation, while shared perforant path input to both subfields produces the 0-msec synchronous correlation.
span.quote: Synchronous activity (0-msec differential) indicates common input, consistent with perforant path projections to both CA3 and CA1. Feed-forward short-lag (2–5 msec) correlation is consistent with correctly categorized CA1 and CA3 neurons connected monosynaptically by Schaffer collateral projections.

span.label: Only the 2-5 msec feed-forward correlations can be taken as definitive evidence of CA3-to-CA1 synaptic connectivity; the synchronous and long-lag pairs are inferred to be correctly assigned rather than proven so.
span.quote: While only the 2- to 5-msec feed-forward correlations (20.3%) can be definitively identified as CA3-to- CA1 synaptic connectivity, the predominance of positive correlations (77.8%) and infrequent occurrence of inverse correlations suggest that the synchronous and multisynaptic correlate cell pairs are correctly identified with respect to CA3 and CA1 localization, and are further consistent with known common projections from entorhinal cortex to hippocampus, as well as indirect projections within the CA3 and CA1 cell layers.

span.label: The localization procedure used here is not a standardized stereotactic system, which the authors say would be needed for cross-centre standardization.
span.quote: Localization using standardized temporal stereotactic systems, such as that described by Miller et al.,25 would be useful for future iterations or for standardization across surgical centers.

span.label: A cell type is inferred from a firing-rate threshold and those cells are excluded from the sample.
span.quote: Neurons with steady-state resting firing rates > 20 Hz (i.e., clearly interneurons) were not recorded

span.label: The cell-type labels are confirmed by the connectivity pattern they are used to demonstrate.
span.quote: Cells were selected as candidate CA3 and CA1 principal neurons on the basis of waveform and firing rate characteristics and confirmed within the CA3-to-CA1 neural projection pathways via measures of functional connectivity

span.label: The human proportion is validated by its resemblance to published animal numbers.
span.quote: feed-forward correlation between CA3-CA1 pairs was identified in 1071 (26%) of 4070 total pairs, which favorably compares to reports of 20%–25% feedforward CA3-CA1 correlation noted in published animal studies

span.label: interneurons
span.quote: Neurons with steady-state resting firing rates > 20 Hz (i.e., clearly interneurons) were not recorded

span.label: principal neurons
span.quote: Cells were selected as candidate CA3 and CA1 principal neurons on the basis of waveform and firing rate characteristics and confirmed within the CA3-to-CA1 neural projection pathways via measures of functional connectivity

span.label: functional connectivity
span.quote: Cells were selected as candidate CA3 and CA1 principal neurons on the basis of waveform and firing rate characteristics and confirmed within the CA3-to-CA1 neural projection pathways via measures of functional connectivity

span.label: inverse correlation
span.quote: Misidentification of CA3 and CA1 neuron pairs would be expected to yield a higher percentage of inverse correlation

span.label: synaptic connectivity
span.quote: While only the 2- to 5-msec feed-forward correlations (20.3%) can be definitively identified as CA3-to- CA1 synaptic connectivity

span.label: feed-forward correlations
span.quote: While only the 2- to 5-msec feed-forward correlations (20.3%) can be definitively identified as CA3-to- CA1 synaptic connectivity

span.label: an interneuron, here - A FIRING RATE ABOVE 20 Hz: the classification is made in a parenthesis and acted on in the main clause, so a rate threshold becomes a cell type and then an exclusion, and every proportion in the paper is computed over what remained
span.quote: Neurons with steady-state resting firing rates > 20 Hz (i.e., clearly interneurons) were not recorded

span.label: a CA3 or CA1 principal neuron - CANDIDATE BY WAVEFORM, CONFIRMED BY CONNECTIVITY: the label is assigned from waveform and firing rate and then confirmed by the projection pattern it predicts, so the classification and the finding it supports rest on each other
span.quote: Cells were selected as candidate CA3 and CA1 principal neurons on the basis of waveform and firing rate characteristics and confirmed within the CA3-to-CA1 neural projection pathways via measures of functional connectivity

span.label: the argument for the labels - AN EXPECTED SIGNATURE OF ERROR: misidentification is said to be expected to yield a higher percentage of inverse correlation, so the low inverse rate is offered as evidence the labels are right - sound only if misidentification could not also produce the observed pattern
span.quote: Misidentification of CA3 and CA1 neuron pairs would be expected to yield a higher percentage of inverse correlation

span.label: extends → Ulbert et al., intraoperative layer-specific human hippocampal recordings with postoperative histology
span.quote: Electrophysiological recordings were limited due to anesthesia, and this approach required additional time and risk associated with placing depth electrodes during planned temporal lobe resection.14 In this study we demonstrate a combined imaging and electrophysiological recording methodology that successfully confirms electrode placement within the CA1 and CA3 subfields of the human hippocampus without requiring postoperative histological confirmation.

span.label: feed-forward correlations —operationalised-as→ synaptic connectivity
span.note: holds when: only for correlations in the 2- to 5-msec window
span.quote: While only the 2- to 5-msec feed-forward correlations (20.3%) can be definitively identified as CA3-to- CA1 synaptic connectivity

span.label: t-test
span.quote: There was no significant difference between right and left hippocampal CA1 depths (pairwise t-test, t[45] = 1.86, nonsignificant).

span.label: cross-correlation
span.quote: Proposed CA1 and CA3 neuron pairs were constructed between neurons recorded on the same electrodes, and then cross-correlograms were computed as spike-triggered histograms.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: Sample and match responses exhibit significant firing peaks (Z = [peak within sample or match phase − mean outside of sample and match phases]/standard deviation outside of sample and match phases; significant peak = Z > 3.09).

span.label: p-value
span.quote: Five characteristic correlation patterns were identified by peaks (Z > 3.09, p < 0.001)

span.label: Nearly 80% of putative CA3-to-CA1 cell pairs showed positive cross-correlations compatible with a feed-forward connection, whereas only 2.6% showed inverse (feedback) correlation.
span.quote: Cross-correlation analysis confirmed that nearly 80% of putative CA3-to-CA1 cell pairs exhibited positive correlations compatible with feed-forward connection between the cells, while only 2.6% exhibited feedback (inverse) connectivity.

span.label: Feed-forward correlation was found in 1,071 of 4,070 CA3-CA1 pairs (26%), a rate close to the 20%-25% reported in animal studies, even after synchronous and long-latency correlations were excluded.
span.quote: Even though synchronous and long-latency correlations were excluded, feed-forward correlation between CA3-CA1 pairs was identified in 1071 (26%) of 4070 total pairs, which favorably compares to reports of 20%–25% feedforward CA3-CA1 correlation noted in published animal studies.

span.label: In non-epileptic patients the CA1 region lay at an average depth of 36.06 mm from the outer table of the skull on the left and 34.84 mm on the right.
span.quote: The hippocampal morphometric study revealed that across normal patients, the CA1 region was encountered at an average depth of 36.06 ± 2.88 mm from the outer table of the skull on the left hemisphere, and 34.84 ± 2.78 mm on the right hemisphere.

span.label: Only the 2-5 msec feed-forward correlations (20.3%) are definitive CA3-to-CA1 synaptic connectivity, but positive correlations dominated (77.8%) and inverse correlations were rare, which the authors read as evidence that the cells were correctly assigned to CA3 and CA1.
span.quote: While only the 2- to 5-msec feed-forward correlations (20.3%) can be definitively identified as CA3-to- CA1 synaptic connectivity, the predominance of positive correlations (77.8%) and infrequent occurrence of inverse correlations suggest that the synchronous and multisynaptic correlate cell pairs are correctly identified with respect to CA3 and CA1 localization

span.label: Anterior hippocampal neurons fired mainly at the sample response, whereas posterior hippocampal neurons fired at elevated rates in the interval between the sample and the match responses.
span.quote: These examples demonstrate that putative anterior hippocampal neurons fire primarily in response to sample response, with some firing to the match response. Conversely, putative posterior hippocampal neurons appear to fire at elevated rates between the sample response and match response peaks.

span.label: About five times as many recorded hippocampal neurons fired below 5.0 Hz as fired above 5.0 Hz.
span.quote: Table 3 shows that approximately 5 times as many neurons exhibited firing rates below 5.0 Hz than above 5.0 Hz

span.label: feed-forward monosynaptic (2-5 msec lag) versus feedback (inverse) connectivity
span.term: feed-forward monosynaptic (2-5 msec lag) versus feedback (inverse) connectivity
span.quote: These correlation patterns were consistent with simultaneous driving of CA3 and CA1 (0 msec), feed-forward monosynaptic (2–5 msec) or multisynaptic (> 5 msec) connectivity, no correlation, or feedback connectivity (inverse correlation) incompatible with CA3-to-CA1 synaptic connectivity.

span.label: Delayed-Match-to-Sample (DMS) task
span.quote: Each session consisted of 100 trials involving a “sample” phase in which a single image was presented, a randomized variable delay (1–75 seconds) with no images displayed, and a “match” phase in which the same sample image was displayed along with a randomized number of 1–6 distractor images.

span.label: cross-correlation of spike timing between paired CA3 and CA1 neurons
span.term: cross-correlation of spike timing between paired CA3 and CA1 neurons
span.quote: Proposed CA1 and CA3 neuron pairs were constructed between neurons recorded on the same electrodes, and then cross-correlograms were computed as spike-triggered histograms.

span.label: hippocampal dimensions along the implantation track (MRI morphometry)
span.term: hippocampal dimensions along the implantation track (MRI morphometry)
span.quote: A morphometric survey was performed using 3T MRI scans of hippocampi from the 23 implanted patients, as well as 46 normal (i.e., nonepileptic) patients and 26 patients with a history of epilepsy but no history of depth electrode placement, which provided average dimensions of the hippocampus along typical implantation tracks.

span.label: delay duration and number of distractors in the DMS trial
span.term: delay duration and number of distractors in the DMS trial
span.quote: Each session consisted of 100 trials involving a “sample” phase in which a single image was presented, a randomized variable delay (1–75 seconds) with no images displayed, and a “match” phase in which the same sample image was displayed along with a randomized number of 1–6 distractor images.

span.label: 60-Hz line noise in the recorded signal
span.term: 60-Hz line noise in the recorded signal
span.quote: Each signal was recorded with a 60-Hz hardware notch filter to remove line noise, and then digitally bandpass filtered (500–5000 Hz) to isolate single-neuron action potential waveforms.

span.label: non-implanted comparison patients (46 nonepileptic, 26 epileptic)
span.quote: Confirmation of electrode placement within the CA1 and CA3 subfields was determined by comparison with a morphometric survey of 3-Tesla MRI scans from 46 normal (i.e., nonepileptic) patients and 26 patients with a history of epilepsy but no prior depth electrode implantation

span.label: 2.6% — proportion of CA3-CA1 cell pairs showing feedback (inverse) correlation, taken as the misidentification rate
span.quote: Cross-correlation analysis confirmed that nearly 80% of putative CA3-to-CA1 cell pairs exhibited positive correlations compatible with feed-forward connection between the cells, while only 2.6% exhibited feedback (inverse) connectivity.

span.label: 1071 (26%) of 4070 — number and share of cell pairs showing feed-forward CA3-to-CA1 correlation
span.quote: Even though synchronous and long-latency correlations were excluded, feed-forward correlation between CA3-CA1 pairs was identified in 1071 (26%) of 4070 total pairs, which favorably compares to reports of 20%–25% feedforward CA3-CA1 correlation noted in published animal studies.

span.label: 77.8% — share of CA3-CA1 pairs showing any positive (synchronous, short-lag or long-lag) correlation
span.quote: While only the 2- to 5-msec feed-forward correlations (20.3%) can be definitively identified as CA3-to- CA1 synaptic connectivity, the predominance of positive correlations (77.8%) and infrequent occurrence of inverse correlations suggest that the synchronous and multisynaptic correlate cell pairs are correctly identified with respect to CA3 and CA1 localization

span.label: 36.06 ± 2.88 mm — mean depth of left-hemisphere CA1 from the outer table of the skull in non-epileptic patients
span.quote: The hippocampal morphometric study revealed that across normal patients, the CA1 region was encountered at an average depth of 36.06 ± 2.88 mm from the outer table of the skull on the left hemisphere, and 34.84 ± 2.78 mm on the right hemisphere.

span.label: 744 — number of neurons recorded across the 23 implanted patients (per Table 1)
span.quote: Table 1 summarizes the data gathered from 744 neurons recorded from the 23 patients examined in this study.
